2026-11-01.patch_summary: This patch removes the zonelist_node_idx() helper function from the Linux kernel, which was used to return the index of a node for an entry in the zonelist. The function is deemed unnecessary because it loads the zone from the slot again, which can lead to inconsistencies when memory hotplug rewrites zonelists in place. The patch open-codes the functionality in its two remaining callers, neither of which can race with a rebuild. Additionally, one of the callers has unreachable code due to the conditions under which it is called.

reviews.author: Zi Yan
reviews.summary: Identified the patch as correct and suitable for merge, with no issues or concerns raised.
reviews.raw_body:
On Sat Oct 31, 2026 at 10:13 PM EDT, Gregory Price (Meta) wrote:
> zonelist_node_idx() looks like it returns a field of the zoneref, as
> zonelist_zone_idx() does, but it loads the zone from the slot again.
>
> Memory hotplug rewrites zonelists in place, so a caller that has already
> checked the slot can get a different zone, or the NULL terminator, from
> that second load.
>
> __next_zones_zonelist() and mempolicy_slab_node() had this bug.
>
> Remove the helper and open-code it in its two remaining callers, neither
> of which can race with a rebuild.  local_memory_node() runs either inside
> __build_all_zonelists() or during CPU bring-up, which holds
> cpu_hotplug_lock for write and so excludes mem_hotplug_begin().
>
> The lookup in mpol_misplaced() is unreachable: it needs a policy with
> MPOL_F_MOF but not MPOL_F_MORON, and nothing sets one without the other.
>
> Signed-off-by: Gregory Price (Meta) <gourry@gourry.net>
> ---
>  include/linux/mmzone.h | 6 ------
>  mm/mempolicy.c         | 2 +-
>  mm/page_alloc.c        | 2 +-
>  3 files changed, 2 insertions(+), 8 deletions(-)
>
LGTM.

Reviewed-by: Zi Yan <ziy@nvidia.com>

-- 
Best Regards,
Yan, Zi

2026-11-02.patch_summary: The patch removes the zonelist_node_idx() function, which was unnecessary and introduced a potential bug in memory hotplug rewrites. The function is replaced by open-coding it in its two remaining callers, ensuring that they cannot race with a rebuild.
